clue.text: Imposing woman, active type, hosting comedian

indicators.note: one piece hosting another holds it inside like a guest

parts.note: a doer is an active, energetic sort of person
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A grand lady, the busy sort, has a comic staying at her house.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a dignified, often formidable elderly widow of rank, a classic imposing woman.

clue.text: Suddenly leave club, having paid out, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the whole assembly upside down
the abbreviation for paid goes outside the word for club

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid
a mace is a heavy club

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly walks out of the club, having paid up, upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' in a down clue turns the whole thing upside down; 'having' is only a link, with 'out' saying which piece goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, as if striking camp.

clue.text: Broadly speaking, one finishes off half of Jumbo

definitions.text: Broadly speaking, one finishes off half of Jumbo

parts.words: Broadly speaking, one finishes off half of Jumbo
parts.note: suggests eating half an elephant, but means the end of one of a jumbo jet's broad halves

explanation.surface: Roughly speaking, someone polishes off half an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumbo is a jumbo jet; each wing is broadly a half of the plane, and its outer end finishes it off.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost point of an aircraft's wing finishes off that side of the plane.

clue.text: Old square wanted rock song over, right?

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old fogey wanted the rock number played again, did he?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' rearranges SONG OVER with R. 'wanted' is a link. GROSVENOR Square is a long-established square in London's Mayfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosvenor Square is a historic Mayfair square laid out in the eighteenth century, so it is fairly called old.

clue.text: Managed to restrain old nag

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the word for managed holds the letter

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed to hold back an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrain' puts O inside RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white, and nag is slang for any horse.

clue.text: Opening facility for top clothing models?

definitions.text: Opening facility for top clothing models?

parts.words: Opening facility for top clothing models?
parts.note: reads as a launch venue for leading fashion models, but means the gap in a shirt or top that lets an arm through

explanation.surface: A venue opens for the leading fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top clothing' is garments worn as tops, and 'opening' is a literal hole, not a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The hole in a garment through which the arm passes is an opening provided in shirts and other tops.

clue.text: A heartless lie depresses a party enthusiast

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part pushes down on, sits above, what follows
heartless removes the middle letter of the word for lie

parts.note: fiction is an untrue story, a lie
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A false claim with no heart weighs on a party lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes T from FICTION to leave FICION; 'depresses' puts A FICION above A DO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen and knowledgeable fan of some activity.

clue.text: Fur wrap for shivering leader in E European capital

indicators.note: the fur is wrapped round the other piece, like a stole

parts.note: mink is a fur

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fur stole for someone shivering in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrap for' puts S, from 'leader' of shivering, inside MINK; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Minsk is the capital city of Belarus in eastern Europe.

clue.text: Unacceptable charge to deliver goods

parts.note: behaviour that is off is unacceptable
a load or charge is a burden carried

explanation.surface: Excessive fees for making deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload is to unload cargo, handing over goods from a vehicle.

clue.text: Set me up a beer, or cause resentment

indicators.note: set up, around the word me, says that word is raised and so read upwards in a down clue
up finishes the phrase set up, turning the short word in this down entry

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer

explanation.surface: Buy me a pint, or I'll hold a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set ... up' reverses ME to EM above BITTER, a hoppy British draught beer; 'a' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them resentful and bitter.

clue.text: Intended to make up for lack of success

definitions.text: Intended to make up for lack of success

parts.words: Intended to make up for lack of success
parts.note: describes the kind of prize given to a loser, used as a modifier as in a ... prize

explanation.surface: Something meant to compensate for failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works here as a modifier, as in the prize given to runners-up; the clue is a plain description of that purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort offered to someone after a defeat or failure is meant to make up for it, as with a runner-up's prize.

clue.text: Story involving G-men slightly edited

indicators.note: a light edit reorders a few letters, so the agency's initials are rearranged

parts.note: G-men are agents of the US Federal Bureau of Investigation, the FBI

explanation.surface: A tale about American federal agents has been lightly revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly edited' rearranges FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fib is a small lie, and a story is a common euphemism for a lie told by a child.

clue.text: Shift it back inside for a reason

indicators.note: the reversed short word sits inside the word for shift

parts.note: to shift something is to move it

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: Push it back in, and you'd better have a good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a verb telling you to move something; it is the synonym that does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason that drives someone to act.

clue.text: Exploit quarrel over time for growth

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it

indicators.note: over says the word for quarrel is turned round

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a long-running dispute in the hope of growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' looks like an increase in profits after 'Exploit'; it means a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Milkwort is a small wild plant, and growth here means vegetation or a plant.

clue.text: Up for the cup?

parts.note: suggests fans travelling to a final, but means chasing trophies for their own sake

explanation.surface: Supporters heading to the capital for the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for the cup' is a British phrase for fans travelling to the FA Cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-hunting is the pursuit of prizes and trophies, a pot being slang for a cup.

clue.text: Makeshift way to get over current reasons for dealing

definitions.text: Makeshift way to get over current

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, one reason to deal cards
bridge is another card game that needs cards dealt

explanation.surface: Temporary ways round a problem become reasons to do business.
explanation.walkthrough: PONTOON is the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack; 'current' is the flow of a river, not the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary crossing laid on floating supports lets troops or traffic cross a flowing river.

clue.text: Pop in for Fifties' revival party

definitions.text: Pop in for Fifties' revival party

parts.words: Pop in for Fifties' revival party
parts.note: suggests dropping in to a retro party, but means the popular music such a Fifties-themed party would play

explanation.surface: Drop by a party celebrating the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a verb, visiting briefly; it is popular music, the style that ruled the Fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: This energetic pop style arose in the 1950s and is the soundtrack of any Fifties revival.

clue.text: Severe trial of police in troubled state

indicators.note: the police abbreviation goes in the jumbled letters
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of state are rearranged

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives face a hard ordeal in a country in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'police' is the British CID, a detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial of worth, from the use of acid to test gold.

clue.text: Tidy up all suits on hand to prepare for new action

parts.note: to clear a space is to tidy it up
a full pack of cards holds all four suits, so the packs to hand are the decks

explanation.surface: Sort out the cards in your hand before the next round of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from naval practice of removing clutter from a ship's decks before battle, so it means getting ready for action.

clue.text: Speak sharply and be superior, dismissing fourth objective

indicators.note: dismissing the fourth letter removes it from the word for be superior

parts.note: to excel is to be superior
an aim is an objective

explanation.surface: Snap at someone, act superior and sack the fourth goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing fourth' removes the E in fourth place of EXCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly or sharply.

clue.text: Made selection, putting second first, and had a row

indicators.note: putting the letter first places it before the word for made selection

parts.note: culled means picked out, selected

explanation.surface: Picked a team, put the reserve first, and then argued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... first' sets S before CULLED. 'Row' looks like a quarrel; here it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to propel a boat with oars, so sculled means rowed.

clue.text: Shout about that woman — one likely to be picked?

indicators.note: about means the word for shout goes round the pronoun

parts.note: a cry is a shout
her is a pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Yell about some woman, the one most likely to be chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked' suggests being chosen for a team; the definition is a fruit picked from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a fruit gathered from trees, so it is something picked, a play on being chosen.

clue.text: Abandoning principles of proper setting for this era

indicators.note: a setting surrounds a jewel, so the word for proper is placed round the era's letters

parts.note: decent means proper, respectable
AD, anno Domini, labels dates in the present era

explanation.surface: Giving up on standards of correct staging for modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'setting' reads as theatrical staging, but here one piece is mounted round another.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline, someone who has let standards and principles slide into self-indulgence.

clue.text: Almost succeed in fastening pin

indicators.note: almost means the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to do well is to succeed

explanation.surface: Nearly managed to get the fixing peg in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' removes the final L of DO WELL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden peg used to fasten pieces of wood together.

clue.text: At first, exhibited almost nothing satisfying

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the next word
almost means the word for nothing loses its final letter

parts.note: nought means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: From the start, very little was on show that pleased anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the T from NOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfying in quantity is sufficient or adequate, all that is needed.

clue.text: Rachel, no longer Catholic, converted her elder sister

indicators.note: converted means changed, so the remaining letters are reshuffled
no longer means the abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Rachel left the Catholic Church and became a convert, like her older sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' removes R and C from RACHEL, and 'converted' rearranges AHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Leah is Rachel's older sister, married to Jacob first.

clue.text: Letter from abroad appearing shortly, when expected

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, foreign to English
the initials for estimated time of arrival, given for something due soon

explanation.surface: A letter from overseas should turn up any moment now.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the seventh Greek letter and the abbreviation for the estimated time something will arrive.

clue.text: So one has to do the job without the manual?

definitions.text: So one has to do the job without the manual?

parts.words: So one has to do the job without the manual?
parts.note: suggests working without an instruction booklet, but means work that is not manual labour, office work

explanation.surface: Someone must fix things without the instruction booklet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' looks like a handbook; here it is physical labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Office and professional workers are described this way, as opposed to manual workers in blue collars.

clue.text: Having delay, get mail processed —

indicators.note: processed means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Held up while the post is being sorted, and so...
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges GET MAIL; 'Having' is a link, and the dash runs the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval of delay between one event and another.

clue.text: - leave the rest

definitions.meaning: leave as a noun means time off work
a rest or break from routine, a period of relaxation

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: go away and forget about everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash continues the sentence begun at 27, so 'the rest' looks like 'everything else' but is a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is both leave from work and a period of rest and relaxation.
